rules.quote: Refer to judges of the following courts as ‘Justice’ and use the title ‘The Honourable’:
rules.violation_condition: failing to refer to a judge of the High Court, Federal Court, Federal Circuit and Family Court (Division 1), or state/territory supreme court as 'Justice' or without the title 'The Honourable' (or 'The Hon')
when: Applies to judges of the High Court, Federal Court, Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 1), and state/territory supreme courts.
The term 'Honourable' can also be abbreviated to 'Hon' without a full stop.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: The list under 8db0300710a2 defines the superior courts; block 002af22a2006 restates the exact rule for a subset, and 99a99addb5cd provides an abbreviation permission/variant.

rules.quote: In emails and letters, use ‘Dear Justice [Family name]’ to address:
rules.violation_condition: failing to address a justice of the Federal Circuit and Family Court (Division 1) or state/territory supreme court as 'Dear Justice [Family name]' in correspondence, or failing to conclude correspondence with 'Yours faithfully'
when: Applies to correspondence (emails and letters) addressing a justice of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 1) or a state/territory supreme court judge.
rules.why: G-2: The salutation and sign-off for correspondence to superior court judges form a single unit of correspondence protocol.

covers.quote: Use the titles ‘Your Honour’, ‘His Honour’ or ‘Her Honour’ for judges of:
Use the title ‘His Honour’ or ‘Her Honour’ for judges of these courts.

examples.note: Example of proper form of title for a district/county court judge.
Example of proper form of title for a district/county court judge.

rules.quote: Address judges of the following courts as ‘Judge’:
rules.violation_condition: failing to address a judge of the Federal Circuit and Family Court (Division 2), a district court, or a county court as 'Judge' or using incorrect titles rather than 'His Honour' or 'Her Honour'
when: Applies to judges of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2), district courts, and county courts.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: The introductory rule in ac21626f440b and the specific rules in 4aa61d81d1f7 and f951d4c8b34e govern how judges of Division 2, district, and county courts are addressed.

rules.violation_condition: in correspondence to a judge of Division 2, district, or county courts, failing to open with 'Dear Judge [Family name]' or conclude with 'Yours faithfully'
when: Applies to emails and letters to judges of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2), district courts, and county courts.
rules.why: E-3, G-2: Lead-in line and list items establish correspondence salutation and sign-off conventions.

covers.quote: When addressing an envelope use ‘Her Honour Magistrate’ or ‘His Honour Magistrate’.

examples.note: Example of addressing an envelope to a magistrate.
Example of addressing an envelope to a magistrate.

rules.quote: Address magistrates in court as ‘Your Honour’.When outside court, address them as ‘Magistrate’.
rules.violation_condition: failing to address a magistrate as 'Your Honour' in court or as 'Magistrate' outside court, or failing to use 'Her Honour Magistrate' or 'His Honour Magistrate' when addressing an envelope
when: Applies when addressing magistrates (in court, outside court, or on envelopes).
rules.why: G-2: Forms of address for magistrates across different settings (in court, outside court, envelope addressing).

covers.quote: On subsequent mention, you can use ‘Sir’ or ‘Dame’ and the person’s given name.

examples.note: Example of first mention of a dame judge.

rules.quote: Address a judge who is a knight or dame as ‘The Honourable Sir’ or ‘The Honourable Dame’.
rules.violation_condition: failing to address a knighted judge or dame as 'The Honourable Sir' or 'The Honourable Dame' on first mention, or failing to use 'Sir' or 'Dame' with the given name on subsequent mention
when: Applies when referring to a judge who is a knight or dame.
rules.why: G-2, G-3: Initial title and subsequent reference rule for knighted judges.
